glosses: to toast (grill bread to make toast)
to toast (drink to something)
Variante orthographique de toasteur.

examples.text: Elle avait mis la bouilloire et la cafetière en route et elle glissait des tranches de pain dans le toaster.
Quand le pain est trop vieux, on le prend, puis, on le met dans le toaster.

glosses: Faire griller (une tranche de pain).

examples.text: Elle doit se faire chier à lui toaster les tartines de son petit-déjeuner avant même que le réveil ne sonne, puis à enquiller sur le ménage, […].

glosses: Porter un toast, boire à la santé de quelqu’un.
Bread that has been cooked lightly and browned.

examples.text: I ate a piece of toast for breakfast.
This toast and marmalade tastes heavenly.

Tea was a very special institution, revolving as it did around the ceremony and worship of Toast. In [public schools] where alcohol, tobacco and drugs were forbidden, it was essential that something should take their place as a powerful and public totem of virility and cool. Toast, for reasons lost in time, was the substance chosen.

glosses: A proposed salutation (e.g. saying \"cheers\") while drinking alcohol.

examples.text: At the reception, there were many toasts from the well-wishers.

glosses: A person, group, or notable object to which a salutation with alcohol is made; a person or group held in similar esteem.

examples.text: He was the toast of high society.
Josephine Baker did not become the toast of Paris by just shaking her booty for some theater gypsies as a party wound down.

glosses: Something that is irreparably damaged or used up, especially when destroyed by heat or fire; something which has been burnt to a crisp or incinerated.

examples.text: The metal frame survived the fire, but the plastic and rubber bits are toast.

glosses: Something that will be no more; something subject to impending destruction, harm or injury.

examples.text: to become/be toast
If I ever get my hands on the guy that stole my wallet, he’s toast!
You are going to be toast if you don't submit your school project on time.
This chick is toast!

glosses: A type of extemporaneous narrative poem or rap.
An old toast (\"a lively fellow who drinks excessively\").
A transient, informational unclickable pop-up overlay, less interactive than a snackbar.

examples.text: With the new Windows Push Notification Service, you can remotely send notifications from a cloud-based web service. In Windows 8, the majority of the Toast messages are standard duration toasts.

glosses: A piece of toast.

examples.text: Go, fetch me a quart of Sacke, put a toſt in't.

glosses: to cook lightly by browning via direct exposure to a fire or other heat source

examples.text: We used to enjoy toasting marshmallows around the campfire.

glosses: to cook lightly by browning under a grill or in a toaster; to grill

examples.text: Top with cheese and toast under the grill for a few minutes.

glosses: To engage in a salutation, often with raising of the drinking vessel, while drinking an alcoholic beverage in honor of someone or something.

examples.text: We toasted the happy couple many times over the course of the evening.
You all have achieved so much together thus far, so I think that deserves a toast! Let's toast!

glosses: To warm thoroughly.

examples.text: I toasted my feet by the fire.

glosses: To perform an extemporaneous narrative poem or rap.

examples.text: Toasting over a record does more than change the way that record is perceived by the audience: it creates a new piece of music with joint creative authorship, although the law does not support this characterization.
